learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operation, limitations, and applications of the main robotic sensors.
Integrate sensors into a robotic system, both at the hardware and software level.
Design sensor fusion and state estimation algorithms.
Analyze sensory data and use them for navigation, perception, and control.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to sensing systems for robotics: classification of sensors (active/passive, absolute/incremental), performance parameters (accuracy, resolution, precision), basic concepts of measurement and uncertainty evaluation, hardware and interfacing architectures.
Position, velocity, and orientation sensors: optical and magnetic encoders, IMUs (accelerometers, gyroscopes, magnetometers), inertial measurements, calibration.

Environmental perception: distance sensors (ultrasonic, infrared, LiDAR, ToF), computer vision (RGB, stereo, and RGB-D cameras), introduction to computer vision for robotics, localization and mapping (maps, landmarks, loop closure).
Sensor fusion and state estimation: least squares, Kalman filters, EKF, localization and SLAM algorithms, multi-sensor integration.

Exercises and laboratory sessions: implementation of pipelines for real and simulated sensors, basic use of ROS/ROS2 for data acquisition and management, experiments and exercises with real sensors (IMU, LiDAR, cameras, encoders) and on a robotic platform.

assessment_methods.method: Project (group of two or three, with a 3-4 page report)
Oral examination (open discussion on one or two topics)

assessment_rules: To successfully pass the exam, students must complete a project and an oral examination. The final grade will be based on a weighted evaluation of the project (40%) and the oral exam (60%).
